page: Microsoft Azure D8d_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The configuration includes 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by a 35 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory (4.0 GB per core) and includes 307 GB of local SSD storage.

Performance benchmarks place the D8d_v4 consistently in the average tier across most workloads. Single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, Geekbench scores, and Passmark CPU evaluations all register in the middle 50% category. The system demonstrates solid memory bandwidth, with read-only small block cached memory reaching 414.44 GB/sec and large block uncached writes at 34.22 GB/sec. However, a notable performance tradeoff is observed in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, which falls into the bottom 25% tier with a throughput of 27.25 GB/sec, contrasting with the average-tier single-threaded decompression performance.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D8d_v4 offers a balanced resource density of compute, memory, and local storage, making it a viable option for workloads requiring temporary local storage without the premium of specialized memory or compute-heavy instances. It is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, Redis caching, database operations, and lightweight machine learning tasks such as small-scale LLM inference.
